claim: An independent benchmark (AIMultiple, GPT-4.1, Bright Data MCP) measured 78.5% fewer input tokens with code execution than regular MCP tool calling (165K vs 771K), with both approaches at 100% success, but code execution used 2.2x more output tokens.

evidence.quote: Input token savings: Code execution uses 78.5% fewer input tokens (165K vs 771K):
Higher output tokens: Code execution approach uses 2.2× more output tokens because the model writes code + explanations

claim: Anthropic reports programmatic tool calling cut average tokens 37% (43,588 to 27,297) on complex research tasks, while its docs report that on tau2-bench with 1-2 sequential tool calls per turn it left scores unchanged and cost roughly 8 percent more.

evidence.quote: Average usage dropped from 43,588 to 27,297 tokens, a 37% reduction on complex research tasks.
programmatic tool calling left scores unchanged and cost roughly 8 percent more. Sequential single-call workflows do not benefit.
Programmatic tool calling trades a small fixed overhead (container startup, script generation) for large savings on tool-result tokens and model round-trips.

claim: Cloudflare reports its Code Mode MCP server for the full Cloudflare API uses about 1,000 tokens versus 1.17 million tokens for an equivalent MCP server without Code Mode (99.9%), and its internal portal's 52 tools (about 9,400 tokens) collapse into 2 portal tools using about 600 tokens (94%).

evidence.quote: An equivalent MCP server without Code Mode would consume 1.17 million tokens
those 52 tools collapse into 2 portal tools consuming roughly 600 tokens

claim: Bifrost (Maxim AI) reports Code Mode cut input tokens 58.2% at 96 tools, 84.5% at 251 tools and 92.8% at 508 tools; Anthropic's 150,000-to-2,000-token (98.7%) figure is an illustrative example of progressive tool disclosure, not a benchmarked evaluation.

evidence.quote: In Bifrost's benchmark, Code Mode cut input tokens by 58.2% at 96 tools, 84.5% at 251 tools, and 92.8% at 508 tools, with a 100% pass rate in every round.
This reduces the token usage from 150,000 tokens to 2,000 tokens

claim: A 2026 preprint found programmatic tool calling matches or exceeds native JSON tool calling in 11 of 14 models on BFCL v4; Felendler et al. (2026) found code-execution MCP significantly reduces token usage and latency but introduces a vastly expanded attack surface, identifying 16 attack classes.

evidence.quote: Programmatic tool calling matches or exceeds native JSON tool calling in 11 of 14 models on BFCL v4, with the GPT-5.6 family achieving a 10.6% improvement over the JSON tool calling baseline.
Programmatic tool calling matches or exceeds native JSON tool calling in 11 of 14 models on BFCL v4,
demonstrating that while CE-MCP significantly reduces token usage and execution latency, it introduces a vastly expanded attack surface.
